newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq still working on wheat import tender - trade.
newsitem.headline: Iraq still working on wheat import tender - trade.

text.p: Iraq is expected to decide later on Monday on a tender for the import of 100,000 tonnes of French wheat in March and April, European grain traders said on Monday.
Exporters also expected Iraq to end up buying more wheat from France, possibly as much as 300-350,000 tonnes.
Paris-based Iraqi officials told Reuters talks for the wheat purchase were under way. "Negotiations are still on," one official said.
Iraq, which was reported to have bought 300,000 tonnes of French wheat in December, has since January 14 been negotiating a new purchase of wheat under a United Nations oil-for-food deal.
A first round of talks allowed Iraq to narrow down selling offers, and talks had now entered a second and final stage, traders said.
In the first round of talks Iraq indicated it was eyeing a price tag of $185-$186 per tonne, including cost and freight, for wheat delivery to the Iraqi port of Umm Qasr.
The lowest-priced offers submitted by exporters for that destination stood at $187.50, cost and freight.
"There are sets of prices -- cost and freight for Umm Qasr delivery and delivery Baghdad through Jordan's port of Aqaba, which is more costly," one exporter explained.
But because Umm Qasr had a limited cargo handling capacity, Iraq might seek deliveries to both destinations.
"I expect further details during the day," one exporter said, adding Iraq would like exporters to cut their $187.50 per tonne offer by around $2.
Iraq was reported to have bought 300,000 tonnes of French wheat in December for January and February shipment.

A French budget ministry official confirmed the figure on Monday, saying France had submitted requests to the United Nations for the sale of a total of 300,000 tonnes of wheat to Iraq under a U.N. pact allowing Iraq to buy food and medicines with money raised from oil sales.
The official said U.N. approval was needed for the deals to go ahead.
"There has been no answer from the United Nations. I think the U.N. started reviewing the requests at the end of last week. I am not even sure they will answer this week," he said.

Under a U.N. pact, Iraq can sell oil worth $2 billion in renewable six-month stages. After war reparations and other costs, about half the $2 billion will be available for the purchase of food and medicines,
But contracts with commercial firms must first be passed to the United Nations via national authorities and then approved by a U.N. committee in New York.
European exporters also cited market talk that Iraq might turn to the United States for wheat after completing its second round of French wheat imports.
"Some are already talking of future purchases of U.S. wheat," one French exporter said.
